references.text: Jesus sends Peter and John to prepare the Passover meal and gives them detailed instructions on how to find the place. Verse 13 confirms that they found everything exactly as Jesus had told them ([ref:Luk 22:8-12|Luke 22:8-12]).

The parallel account in Mark's Gospel tells the same story: the disciples went out, came to the city, and found everything just as Jesus had said, and they prepared the Passover meal ([ref:Mark 14:16|Mark 14:16]).
Matthew's parallel account states that the disciples did as Jesus had commanded them and prepared the Passover meal ([ref:Matt 26:19|Matthew 26:19]).

A similar pattern where Jesus sends the disciples with specific instructions (to find a young donkey), and they find everything exactly as he had said. This demonstrates Jesus' prophetic foreknowledge ([ref:Luk 19:32-34|Luke 19:32-34]).

Here too, at the entry into Jerusalem, the disciples are sent by Jesus with detailed instructions and find everything just as he had said. This confirms the same pattern of Jesus' supernatural knowledge ([ref:Mark 11:4-6|Mark 11:4-6]).
An example of Jesus' words being fulfilled and the disciples remembering and believing afterward. Jesus' prophecies prove to be trustworthy and reliable ([ref:Joh 2:22|John 2:22]).

The preparation of the Passover lamb in the original Passover celebration in Egypt, which forms the basis for the Jewish Passover that the disciples are now preparing ([ref:2 Mos 12:3-6|Exodus 12:3-6]).

The command to celebrate Passover as a memorial of the exodus from Egypt. The disciples' preparation of the Passover meal in Luke 22:13 was carried out in accordance with these Old Testament regulations ([ref:5 Mos 16:1-3|Deuteronomy 16:1-3]).
